item.title: Intervenção da PSP põe fim a acampamentos pela habitação em Lisboa e no Porto
item.snippet: A intervenção policial nas praças do Rossio, em Lisboa, e Dom João I, no Porto, resultou na detenção de 55 manifestantes e gerou debate sobre os limites da lei.
body: A Polícia de Segurança Pública pôs fim na madrugada aos acampamentos de protesto pelo direito à habitação que concentravam dezenas de pessoas em Lisboa e no Porto. A operação policial resultou na detenção de 55 manifestantes na capital por crime de desobediência, após três avisos prévios para que abandonassem o local e retirassem as tendas.

Enquanto no Porto a saída dos manifestantes ocorreu de forma voluntária e sem incidentes após negociação com as autoridades, em Lisboa registaram-se momentos de tensão e empurrões. A direcção nacional da PSP defendeu que a atuação foi adequada, calma e proporcional.

Vogais e especialistas em direito constitucional apontam para a delicada linha entre a garantia da liberdade de reunião e a manutenção da ordem pública em democracias liberais, num momento em que a crise da habitação continua a mobilizar a sociedade.
more: A polémica gerada em torno da desocupação levou vários partidos e figuras públicas a debaterem a proporção da força policial utilizada. O porta-voz da PSP rejeitou qualquer tipo de carga policial ou uso de bastões, sublinhando que a avaliação de risco foi feita de forma contínua antes de avançar para a praça.

Por sua vez, movimentos cívicos e associações de defesa da habitação criticaram duramente a actuação das autoridades, lembrando que o protesto pacífico é um pilar fundamental da participação cívica. Parte dos detidos deverá ser libertada ao longo do dia, enquanto continuam marcadas novas formas de contestação para os próximos tempos.

item.title: Quando o Sporting processou o Público num caso que durou quatro anos
item.snippet: Uma retrospetiva judicial recorda o processo de 2001 em que o clube de Alvalade exigiu milhões ao jornal devido a notícias sobre as suas finanças.
body: Em Fevereiro de 2001, o jornal PÚBLICO publicou artigos sobre dívidas fiscais de vários clubes portugueses, incluindo uma referência a valores em falta por parte do Sporting Clube de Portugal. O clube liderado na altura não tardou a reagir judicialmente.

Considerando que a honra da instituição tinha sido manchada, o clube avançou com um processo contra o jornal e três dos seus jornalistas, exigindo uma indemnização de 2,5 milhões de euros por danos morais.

O lituano desfecho nos tribunais só viria a acontecer anos mais tarde, em Abril de 2005, marcando um dos capítulos mais mediáticos na relação entre a imprensa escrita e as altas instâncias do futebol nacional.
more: O caso faz parte de uma série de episódios jurídicos e políticos marcantes revisitados pela imprensa para analisar os limites entre o jornalismo de investigação, o segredo de justiça e a litigância de má-fé por parte de entidades influentes.

A análise destes processos históricos sublinha a importância da protecção legal da atividade jornalística num ecossistema democrático onde o escrutínio das contas de clubes com relevância pública continua a ser um tema sensível.

item.title: Metro da Margem Sul avança para greve prolongada até final de outubro
item.snippet: Trabalhadores da MTS exigem novos acordos salariais e melhores condições laborais, antevendo dias de grande transtorno para quem atravessa o Tejo.
body: Os utentes dos transportes públicos na Margem Sul vão enfrentar uma semana particularmente difícil devido à greve total e parcial convocada pelos trabalhadores da Metro Transportes do Sul (MTS). A paralisação afeta diretamente os concelhos de Almada e Seixal.

Após dois anos e meio de negociações infrutíferas para um novo Acordo de Empresa, o sindicato avançou para a greve para contestar a falta de respostas às reivindicações de atualização salarial e melhores condições de organização do trabalho.

A empresa já veio classificar a greve como desproporcional, assegurando que mantém a disponibilidade para negociar, mas foram salvaguardados apenas alguns serviços mínimos essenciais nas horas de ponta.
more: Com o trânsito rodoviário sob forte pressão adicional e alternativas de transporte reduzidas, aconselha-se aos passageiros que planeiem com antecedência as suas deslocações diárias para Lisboa.

A paralisação junta-se a um mês de outubro particularmente agitado no setor dos transportes na região de Lisboa, refletindo o descontentamento laboral generalizado em várias frentes de mobilidade urbana.

item.title: Falha técnica deixa serviços e cartões da Revolut indisponíveis
item.snippet: Uma paragem técnica deixou a aplicação da Revolut inoperacional, afetando pagamentos e levantamentos.
body: Os utilizadores da Revolut enfrentam dificuldades no acesso a fundos devido a uma falha técnica que deixou a aplicação bancária inoperacional em Portugal e noutros mercados.
A interrupção comprometeu transações essenciais, incluindo pagamentos com cartões, levantamentos em caixas automáticas e transferências bancárias, gerando alertas de erro aos clientes.
more: A empresa britânica confirmou a indisponibilidade parcial das suas funcionalidades centrais, assegurando contudo que os saldos e as informações pessoais dos clientes permanecem totalmente seguros e protegidos.
Embora a plataforma tenha registado perturbações significativas, a equipa técnica trabalhou para restabelecer a normalidade e mitigar o impacto nos milhares de utilizadores afetados pela falha.

item.title: Presidente da CIP critica protestos e defende o crescimento económico
item.snippet: Armindo Monteiro criticou a minoria ruidosa nos protestos pela habitação e apelou a um pacto social.
body: O presidente da CIP, Armindo Monteiro, criticou a minoria ruidosa responsável pelos protestos pela habitação, defendendo que a rua não resolve nem aproxima as soluções necessárias.
Numa declaração em Lisboa, o líder patronal sustentou que a resposta ao aumento do custo de vida passa pelo crescimento económico e pelo aumento da riqueza do país.
more: Monteiro opôs uma maioria silenciosa, que trabalha diariamente, às formas de contestação mais visíveis, alertando para o risco de confrontos.
Apesar de demonstrar respeito por quem participa nos acampamentos, o responsável insistiu que o caminho ideal reside na cooperação institucional e na concertação social.

item.title: Diogo Moreira na equipa oficial Honda de MotoGP em 2027
item.snippet: O piloto brasileiro vai integrar a equipa oficial da Honda no Mundial de Velocidade a partir de 2027.
body: O brasileiro Diogo Moreira vai juntar-se a Fabio Quartararo na equipa oficial Honda no Mundial de MotoGP em 2027, num contrato plurianual anunciado pelo construtor japonês.
A promoção à estrutura principal acontece após a sua estreia na categoria rainha pela LCR Honda, onde se destacou ao conquistar um pódio numa corrida sprint no Japão.
more: O jovem piloto de 22 anos, campeão mundial de Moto2 em 2025, afirmou realizar um sonho de infância ao integrar a Honda HRC Castrol.
Esta mudança insere-se na preparação para a entrada em vigor dos novos regulamentos técnicos previstos para 2027, com o objetivo de devolver a marca japonesa aos triunfos.

item.title: Tendas retiradas em Lisboa e Porto após intervenção da PSP
item.snippet: A polícia retirou as tendas dos manifestantes no Rossio e na Praça D. João I, com novas protestos previstos.
body: A PSP procedeu à retirada das tendas montadas por manifestantes nas acampadas da Praça D. João I, no Porto, e no Rossio, em Lisboa, numa operação realizada durante a madrugada.
Enquanto no Porto a ordem foi cumprida sem grande oposição, em Lisboa registaram-se detenções durante a intervenção policial que desmantelou os acampamentos.
more: A ação das autoridades gerou forte repercussão pública no âmbito dos protestos contra a crise na habitação que têm marcado a atualidade nacional.
Os movimentos organizadores convocaram novas concentrações e manifestações para o final do mesmo dia em ambas as cidades.

item.title: Apreensões de cocaína aumentam 68% em Portugal face a 2025
item.snippet: Polícia Judiciária revela que o país já apreendeu 42 toneladas de cocaína ao longo deste ano.
body: As autoridades policiais portuguesas já apreenderam 42 toneladas de cocaína, um valor que representa um aumento de 68% em comparação com o total registado no ano passado.
O anúncio foi feito pelo diretor nacional da Polícia Judiciária, Carlos Cabreiro, durante as celebrações do aniversário da instituição, destacando o esforço conjunto das forças de segurança.
more: Cabreiro sublinhou a cooperação entre diferentes entidades e as Forças Armadas no combate ao tráfico internacional de estupefacientes.
Durante o evento, o responsável abordou também os desafios colocados pela inteligência artificial e reafirmou a solidez da estrutura da Polícia Judiciária.

item.title: Carneiro classifica lei das rendas como desumana e injusta
item.snippet: O secretário-geral do PS apelou ao primeiro-ministro para que deixe cair a nova legislação sobre arrendamento.
body: O secretário-geral do Partido Socialista, José Luís Carneiro, classificou a nova lei das rendas como desumana e injusta, apelando ao Governo para reconsiderar a proposta.
Durante uma visita a projetos de habitação no Algarve, o líder socialista criticou a facilitação de despejos e defendeu limites claros para os encargos familiares.
more: O PS propôs como alternativa a criação de uma garantia pública para proteger inquilinos vulneráveis e jovens, assegurando também maior segurança aos senhorios.
Carneiro reforçou a necessidade de expandir a oferta pública de habitação e criticou os valores de referência considerados moderados pelo Executivo.

item.title: Anthropic and Nscale in Talks for Another Massive Compute Deal
item.snippet: Just a month after a $45 billion agreement, Anthropic and Nscale are reportedly discussing a second massive compute deal.
body: Anthropic and infrastructure provider Nscale are reportedly in talks for another massive $45 billion compute deal, according to Bloomberg sources. This potential agreement follows closely on the heels of a similarly sized partnership announced just over a month ago.

The staggering sums being injected into AI infrastructure continue to unnerve some investors who question whether the massive spending will yield proportional profits. Despite these concerns, Anthropic is pressing forward as both companies work toward upcoming IPO plans.
more: The relentless expansion of compute capacity underscores the intense resource race among frontier AI labs. While critics worry about a potential bubble fueled by exorbitant hardware costs, companies like Anthropic maintain that massive scaling is essential for future model capabilities.

Meanwhile, Nscale has encountered some investor pushback regarding its targeted $30 billion valuation ahead of its public debut, highlighting the shifting financial climate for infrastructure providers in the current AI boom.

item.title: The Creepy, Beautiful Digital Art Behind the New Clayface Poster
item.snippet: Illustrator Estevan Silveira blends comic style with classic body horror for a striking new movie poster.
body: The upcoming DC film featuring Matt Hagen's Clayface is leaning heavily into body horror, and its promotional campaign is matching that energy. A new poster created by illustrator Estevan Silveira has been turning heads with its intricate and unsettling visual details.

The artwork depicts the hunched, melting form of Clayface clutching his head, set against grungy red backgrounds with retro creature-feature vibes. Fans online have praised the piece for offering a refreshing alternative to standard floating-head movie posters.
more: The striking interplay of sickly yellow-and-green tones against deep reds gives the poster a distinct retro horror aesthetic that has resonated deeply with comic and movie fans alike.

In an era where blockbuster marketing often relies on generic digital composites, this detailed illustrative approach highlights the enduring power of strong, character-driven concept art in modern film branding.

item.title: Fifty Shades of Hay: Wicker Parodies Bodice-Ripper Romances
item.snippet: The new film poster for Wicker cleverly mimics vintage paperback romance novels with a woody twist.
body: The upcoming film Wicker has leaned into its eccentric premise with a new poster that parodies classic, raunchy romance novel covers. Featuring lead actress Olivia Colman embraced by Alexander Skarsgård in sentient wicker form, the design hits all the right nostalgic notes.

Framed by rich jewel tones and elegant gold script typography, the artwork mimics vintage mass-market paperbacks while maintaining a surprisingly sophisticated visual standard. Fans quickly dubbed the clever pastiche 'Fifty Shades of Hay'.
more: By subverting the visual tropes of 80s and 90s bodice-rippers, the marketing team turned what could have been a standard comedic poster into a piece of clever visual culture commentary.

The intricate typography and classical portrait composition elevate the joke, proving that genre parodies can still achieve genuine aesthetic merit when executed with a careful eye for historical design details.

item.title: An Existential Spiral Over Video Call Appearance Filters
item.snippet: A sick morning meeting prompts a reflection on the creeping ubiquity of digital beauty filters in the workplace.
body: Logging into a work meeting while battling a cold, one writer was met with a prompt familiar to many remote workers: 'Touch up your appearance?' What followed was an unexpected dive into video platform beauty filters and the subtle ways digital alterations have infiltrated professional spaces.

While social media filters have long been recognized for warping self-image and contributing to body dysmorphia, seeing them applied to everyday work calls blurs the line between reality and digital performance even further.
more: The experience raises quiet questions about workplace pressures and the implicit expectation to look permanently polished, even when dealing with ordinary human illnesses.

Moreover, the observation that these automated touch-up tools lean heavily toward traditional makeup aesthetics—often without equivalent options for masculine-leaning users—reveals how software defaults quietly encode societal assumptions about appearance.

item.title: Spotify Expands Paid Podcast Memberships Globally
item.snippet: Creators can now offer bonus content, ad-free listening, and exclusive perks through new subscription tiers.
body: Spotify is rolling out paid podcast memberships to 34 markets globally, giving creators a new way to monetize their core audiences beyond traditional ad revenue. Eligible podcasters can now offer tiered perks including bonus episodes, early access, and reduced ads.
The feature arrives as Spotify continues to invest heavily in its platform ecosystem, offering creators control over pricing and packaging while taking a ten percent cut of membership revenue.
more: To qualify for the program, creators must meet specific engagement thresholds and host their shows on designated platforms like Spotify for Creators or Megaphone.

By shifting exclusive purchases to the web rather than in-app ecosystems, Spotify is attempting to build a sustainable alternative revenue model that directly rivals other major media hosting networks.

item.title: Exploring Retro Animation Styles in After Effects
item.snippet: A motion designer shares a sneak peek of a fun, nostalgic project built in After Effects.
body: An independent motion designer has offered a glimpse into an ongoing personal project titled 'The Modern World,' showcasing a distinct retro animation aesthetic built inside After Effects.
The short showcase highlights playful character styling and classic frame-by-frame texturing techniques that bring a warm, hand-crafted feel to digital motion work.
more: Projects like this often rely on a mix of shape layers, custom expression setups, and vintage color grading to achieve an authentic mid-century or retro look without leaving the timeline.
Sharing work-in-progress clips within community spaces continues to be a great way for motion designers to trade workflow tips, experiment with niche styles, and gather feedback from peers.

item.title: Good design communicates how things work without needing instructions.
item.snippet: Everyday objects should make their functions clear through affordances and feedback, removing the frustration of human error.
body: Don Norman's classic explores why some objects satisfy us effortlessly while others cause endless frustration. He argues that bad design is usually the result of a mismatch between how a device works and how people naturally think it should work. By focusing on fundamental psychological principles like visibility, feedback, and mental models, creators can build products that feel intuitive and human-centered.

For anyone shaping visual experiences or physical spaces, this book is a gentle reminder that the user's struggle is almost always a design failure, not a personal one. It encourages a deep empathy for how people actually interact with the world around them.

book.title: The Design of Everyday Things
book.author: Don Norman

lessons.title: Affordances suggest action
lessons.text: Physical objects should naturally signal how they can be used. A flat plate on a door invites pushing, while a handle invites pulling, eliminating the need for instructional signs.

lessons.title: Feedback prevents confusion
lessons.text: Every action requires immediate and clear feedback so the user knows the system received their command. Without it, people repeat actions unnecessarily and lose trust.

lessons.title: Mapping bridges intention and effect
lessons.text: Good spatial mapping ensures that controls correspond clearly to their intended results. When a row of stove switches maps logically to the burners, errors drop significantly.

lessons.title: Embrace human error
lessons.text: People will inevitably make mistakes, so systems must be designed to tolerate them. Treat errors as valuable feedback on where the design itself can be improved.

book.takeaway: Walk around your workspace this week and identify one object that constantly frustrates you, then map out how a simple design change could fix it.
book.forWho: Motion designers and creators who want to build more intuitive and human-friendly experiences.

item.title: A Christian Dad Takes On a 14-Foot Halloween Demon
item.snippet: An Ohio father's impassioned LinkedIn rant about a terrifying neighborhood lawn display inadvertently amused the internet.
body: Halloween brings out all kinds of seasonal decor, but a 14-foot demon holding a bloody axe proved to be a bridge too far for one father of two. In a viral LinkedIn post, Colin Stroud vented about the spooky setup disrupting his family's neighborhood walks and keeping his four-year-old daughter awake at night.

Rather than just asking the neighbor to tone it down, the dad offered an unexpected silver lining. He claimed the terrifying ordeal served as a powerful 'faith activation' that brought his young children closer to God.
more: Naturally, social media users had a field day with the logic, offering up endless sarcastic reactions to the idea that giant lawn demons are a legitimate parenting tool.
While some parents sympathized with the difficulty of explaining neighborhood spooks to sensitive toddlers, the dramatic framing turned the local dispute into pure internet comedy.

item.title: The Mystery of the Oldest Surviving American Flag
item.snippet: Hidden in a Massachusetts town lies the Bedford Flag, an ornate crimson banner that may have seen the opening shots of the Revolution.
body: In a small historic town just outside Boston sits the Bedford Flag, recognized as the oldest complete surviving flag in the United States. Featuring an ornate crimson silk damask background adorned with grapes and pomegranates, the banner depicts an armored hand grasping a sword from a cloud beneath the motto Vince Aut Morire, or Conquer or Die.

Though experts place its creation in the early 1700s based on its unique pigments and design, the exact maker remains a mystery. Records suggest minuteman Nathaniel Page may have carried it straight into the Battles of Lexington and Concord in 1775.
more: For generations, the flag remained in the Page family before being handed over to the town in 1885. Today, visitors can still view the delicate relic by requesting the key to the town's dedicated Flag Room.
The striking design lives on locally, appearing on police and fire department uniforms, town seals, and reenactor parades every Patriots' Day.

item.title: A $6 Time Capsule of Early American Life in Rhode Island
item.snippet: The Paine House Museum preserves centuries of local history inside a structure that started as a humble one-room sawmill home.
body: Tucked off a Rhode Island highway sits the Paine House Museum, a living snapshot of early American domestic life. Originally built in the late 1600s by Samuel Bennett to support his local sawmill, the building slowly evolved over the centuries as successive owners added their own architectural touches.
Last lived in during the 1940s, the house now serves as a modest museum where visitors can step back in time for a nominal fee and observe how much living standards have shifted.
more: Visiting requires a bit of local navigation, including finding street parking carefully away from the nearby fire station and residential bottlenecks.
During warmer months, the grounds occasionally host a local farmer's market, blending community charm with a tangible connection to early colonial craftsmanship.

item.title: What Colonial Williamsburg Ate Before Pancakes Ruled
item.snippet: Long before modern syrup-drenched breakfasts, early American mornings relied on coarse cornmeal and kitchen leftovers.
body: Today, Williamsburg is famously packed with pancake houses and breakfast festivals, but mornings 250 years ago looked drastically different. For working-class settlers and enslaved laborers in colonial Virginia, breakfast was an absolute necessity rather than a leisurely culinary event.

Because wheat flour was an expensive luxury reserved for the elite, common tables relied heavily on corn. Cooks prepared simple hoecakes by mixing coarse cornmeal with water, salt, and lard, often cooking them over an open hearth using whatever metal tool was close at hand.
more: When time allowed, breakfast often doubled as a practical way to clear out yesterday's menu, pairing fresh hoecakes with whatever survived the previous night's dinner.
Meanwhile, wealthy aristocrats enjoyed a much slower, refined morning routine featuring boiled milk and leisurely pacing, proving that historical breakfast divides ran deep.

item.title: The Chance 1962 Encounter That Made Tom Petty a Musician
item.snippet: A ten-year-old Tom Petty traded his slingshot for vinyl records after a brief backstage meeting with Elvis Presley.
body: Before leading the Heartbreakers and rocking alongside Bob Dylan, Tom Petty's entire life trajectory was altered by a single afternoon in 1962. While visiting his uncle on the Florida set of an Elvis Presley film, young Petty joined the crowds peering through a chain-link fence.

After slipping into a backstage area, he caught a glimpse of the King of Rock and Roll, who briefly stopped to say hello. That fleeting encounter sparked an obsessive love for music that instantly changed his priorities.
more: Upon returning home, Petty promptly traded his prized aluminum slingshot for a box of vinyl 45s and began obsessively playing records.
He later reflected on how difficult it was to source music history back then, eventually mailing away to England just to secure a copy of The Elvis Presley Handbook.

item.title: Sweden's Giant Concrete Tribute to Vinegar
item.snippet: A 16-foot replica of a classic glass bottle stands as a quirky roadside monument to a southern Swedish town's industrial past.
body: In the small Swedish town of Perstorp, local acetic acid production has roots stretching back to 1881, when factories began utilizing raw materials from surrounding beech forests. To honor that heritage, the town unveiled a massive 16-foot concrete replica of its iconic glass vinegar bottle complete with a bright red cap.
Positioned right beside a main road near the train station, the oversized landmark serves as an unmistakable local symbol and a playful nod to everyday kitchen staples.
more: Unveiled in 1994 by a prominent television chef, the monument even doubles as a practical guide for visitors.
Laminated panels mounted directly on the giant bottle offer traditional cucumber-pickling tips alongside handy travel recommendations for the local municipality.

item.title: Booms & Shakes: October's strategy power moves and the return of human craft
item.snippet: Major creative agencies are doubling down on human-led strategy and craft rather than AI specialists as the industry restructures.
body: October's biggest creative industry movers and shakes reveal a clear trend toward restructuring and a renewed focus on strategy. Agencies like Landor, Small World, and Dalziel & Pow have all recently appointed top-level strategy leads.

Interestingly, none of the recent press releases mentioned 'AI specialists.' Instead, the industry is leaning heavily into human-led craft, responsible AI use, and detailed campaign measurement to prove their value to clients.
more: The shift also includes significant agency consolidation, such as The Chase acquiring Squad in Manchester and York's Say Yes and Verse merging into COMMON.

Meanwhile, studios like ustwo are appointing former creative technologists as engineering leads, highlighting a growing industry consensus that creativity remains a crucial soft skill for technical leadership.

item.title: Is a high-production movie trailer the new portfolio for graphic designers?
item.snippet: A visual designer's viral 8K short film about beating AI and portofolio fatigue has sparked intense debate.
body: In an era where traditional portfolios and social media feeds struggle to stand out against AI-generated content, visual designer Darshita Patankar took a radically different approach to finding work.

Instead of a standard website, she teamed up with her brother to produce a sleek, four-minute cinematic film titled 'Design is Dead,' showcasing her early roots in MS Paint, her design philosophy, and her custom typefaces.
more: The ambitious project has ignited discussions across the design community regarding whether high-production video marketing is becoming a necessary tool for freelancers.
Beyond the flashy format, the video's core message argues that design should remain a fundamental core of brand decision-making rather than just a superficial output.

item.title: DaVinci Resolve Studio drops price in a rare 20% discount
item.snippet: Blackmagic Design has slashed the price of its full studio package for the first time since late 2024.
body: Known as an industry standard for Hollywood color-grading and timeline editing, DaVinci Resolve Studio rarely sees price cuts due to its already reasonable one-off purchase model.
Blackmagic Design has temporarily reduced the full studio package from $295 to $236, offering a rare entry point for creators looking to escape subscription software models.
more: Alongside robust video tools, the software now features a dedicated Photo Page, bringing node-based color grading and raw image editing capabilities to still photography as an alternative to Lightroom.
With annual updates that include new AI tools and audio editing via Fairlight, it remains one of the most comprehensive multimedia suites on the market.

item.title: Cricut's StickerPix combines printing, laminating, and cutting
item.snippet: Cricut's new compact device rolls multiple sticker-making steps into one machine, but comes with a notable catch.
body: Cricut is best known for precision cutters, but their new StickerPix Print + Cut aims to solve the cumbersome multi-step process of making stickers at home.
The compact box integrates printing, laminating, and precision cutting into a single workflow that outputs crisp, colour-accurate sheets in under a minute.
more: Available in different tiers, the beginner model restricts users to pre-made templates, while the higher-end version allows full custom shape cutting.
Despite its user-friendly design and quick output, locked-in proprietary materials and ongoing ink costs mean users will need to weigh convenience against long-term expenses.

item.title: In Clubland: Documenting 35 years of rave and superclub culture
item.snippet: Photographer Mark McNulty's new book captures four decades of dance music history from acid house onwards.
body: Liverpool photographer Mark McNulty has spent decades documenting the evolution of UK club culture, capturing moments from the early days of acid house through the superclub boom.
His upcoming book, In Clubland: 35 Summers of Love, compiles over 550 photographs across 240 pages, offering an unfiltered look at the energy of youth and nightlife.
more: Published by Modern Sky, the book coincides with McNulty's exhibition at Tate Britain as part of the British Culture Archive's showcase on 90s art and fashion.

Before finding his calling behind the lens, McNulty briefly played in a local band alongside future members of Pulp and The Stone Roses before realizing his fifteen minutes on stage were better spent documenting the scene.

item.title: Final Fantasy Resonance brings HD-2D visuals to a classic franchise
item.snippet: Square Enix applies its stunning HD-2D Unreal Engine 5 technology to a new turn-based JRPG.
body: Square Enix continues to experiment with its distinctive HD-2D graphic style, which pairs pixelated 2D characters with lush, dimensional 3D environments rendered in bold color palettes.
While previous iterations graced titles like Octopath Traveler, Final Fantasy Resonance adapts the aesthetic to a new turn-based adventure with dynamic camera movements.
more: The game moves beyond traditional isometric perspectives, occasionally shifting the camera closer to ground level during town exploration to use depth-of-field effects.
Built on Unreal Engine 5, the release opens up exciting visual possibilities for how the studio might revisit its vast retro back catalogue in the future.

item.title: Apple's $3,000 Studio Display XDR: Bright, beautiful, and niche
item.snippet: Apple has expanded its high-end monitor lineup with a feature-packed 120Hz mini-LED screen built specifically for professionals.
body: The new Studio Display XDR sits at the very top of Apple's monitor range, bringing a 5K resolution, massive mini-LED brightness, and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate to professional desks. It packs a surprising amount of internal hardware, including six speakers, three microphones, and a Center Stage camera.
While the build quality and color coverage are exceptional, the steep price tag and strict compatibility with Apple's latest Macs mean it will likely remain a rare sight in most standard studios.
more: Retaining the sleek aluminum profile of its predecessor, the XDR version adds two powered Thunderbolt 5 ports and a height-adjustable stand as standard. For creative professionals relying on color accuracy, the expansive color gamut and deep contrast make it a powerful tool, even if the investment requires careful consideration.

item.title: Can a security-style hologram keep your face out of AI models?
item.snippet: UnitedUs has designed a new visual identity for Twinnin centered around a verified human trust mark.
body: As generative AI makes mimicking voices and likenesses terrifyingly easy, a consent registry called Twinnin has undergone a complete rebrand to make human verification feel tangible. Brighton agency UnitedUs crafted an identity built around a clear choice: license your likeness or defend it.
The resulting logo borrows technical coordinates from facial recognition software and renders them as shimmering, three-dimensional badges reminiscent of security holograms on software packaging.
more: The design relies on immediate psychological association, using familiar security cues to make data ownership transparent. By boiling the complex legalities of digital consent down to straightforward trust markers, the branding gives individuals a distinct way to signal their boundaries in an automated world.

item.title: Stupid Never Dies: When anime, punk, and pop art collide
item.snippet: This chaotic action RPG mashes up graphic design and stop-motion aesthetics, but struggles beneath its vibrant surface.
body: Built in Unreal Engine 5, the art direction of Stupid Never Dies is an aggressive, fizzy mash-up of anime, manga, punk rock, and scrapbooking aesthetics. It feels akin to throwing Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse and Persona 5 into a blender with a stack of nineties zines.
Despite its striking visual personality and zippy combat transformations, the game's repetitive loops and awkward targeting can occasionally overshadow its brilliant style.
more: The visual world-building leans heavily into chaotic textures and maximalist color palettes, proving once again that unique stylistic execution can carry a project's atmosphere even when underlying mechanics feel overly familiar.

item.title: Can Google's new desktop OS bridge the mobile app gap?
item.snippet: The high-end Googlebook brings Android applications to a desktop environment, but creative software still lags behind.
body: Google's latest attempt at a desktop operating system fuses Chrome's DNA with Android, letting users run mobile apps in resizable windows with full mouse support. Built on premium hardware with OLED screens and robust processors, it aims to carve out space alongside traditional laptops.
For creative workflows, running mobile versions of editing tools offers a glimpse of the future, though full desktop-tier video editing remains a notable limitation of the current software ecosystem.
more: Hardware-wise, devices like Acer's iteration lean into understated industrial design, complete with subtle glowing indicator bars. While first-generation growing pains are apparent, future updates could position these hybrid machines as serious contenders for creative professionals on the move.

item.title: Finding accidental beauty in awkward Facebook Marketplace listings
item.snippet: Graphic designer Casey Roarty is turning harsh flash photography and compressed second-hand items into fine art.
body: Hours of scrolling through second-hand listings often reveal a surreal gallery of awkward crops, domestic lighting, and accidental reflections. When designer Casey Roarty moved house, he began cataloging these strange, unintentionally poetic digital artifacts for a personal project titled Is This Still Available?
In an era where hyper-polished, AI-generated imagery is frictionless to produce, these raw, human-shot photos offer a refreshing counter-narrative steeped in genuine imperfection.
more: The project highlights the soft, painterly qualities introduced by heavy image compression and hastily snapped photos of vintage toys or warped fancy dress costumes. By extracting these forgotten snapshots from their practical e-commerce context, Roarty celebrates the unscripted visual culture of the internet.

item.title: Building believable fantasy worlds through consistent internal logic
item.snippet: Environment concept artist Oliver Chen breaks down how magical resources should dictate architectural design.
body: When designing fictional environments, every architectural detail should reflect the underlying rules of the setting. In a recent world-building project centered around a town powered by star sand condensed from starlight, the local architecture and glowing chimneys were explicitly tailored to merge technology with faith.
Using 3D tools like Daz Studio and Blender for initial composition and lighting helps establish spatial consistency before diving into detailed digital painting.
more: By leaning on 3D asset libraries for base structures, artists can focus their energy on atmospheric effects, textures, and small props that make a scene feel truly lived-in. Grounding fantasy elements in logical systems ensures the final concept art feels cohesive and believable to the viewer.

item.title: Estudantes protestam contra a proposta de descongelamento das propinas
item.snippet: Associações de estudantes manifestaram-se em Lisboa contra a intenção do Governo de atualizar o valor máximo das propinas a partir de 2027/2028.
body: Estudantes do ensino superior juntaram-se em protesto frente à sede do Governo, em Lisboa, para contestar a proposta de Orçamento do Estado que prevê o descongelamento das propinas no ensino superior a partir do ano letivo de 2027/2028.

A medida estipula que o limite máximo das propinas nas licenciaturas e cursos técnicos seja atualizado com base na taxa de inflação, pondo fim a um período de congelamento que vigorava desde 2020 e fixava o teto nos 697 euros.
more: Os representantes estudantis criticam o impacto financeiro desta alteração para quem frequenta o ensino superior. A proposta governamental abrange também mestrados profissionalizantes, enquanto outros ciclos de estudos passam a ter propinas alinhadas com o custo real da formação.

Dados associados às receitas das instituições indicam um aumento substancial nas verbas geradas internamente pelas escolas, refletindo a transição de um modelo com maior suporte público para um financiamento complementar mais dependente das receitas próprias.

item.title: Porto de Leixões aposta em eletrificação para descarbonizar navios
item.snippet: Concurso de 7,2 milhões de euros financia sistemas de energia elétrica em terra para embarcações atracadas.
body: O programa Sustentável 2030 lançou um concurso no valor de 7,2 milhões de euros para instalar sistemas de fornecimento de eletricidade a partir de terra em vários terminais do Porto de Leixões.
Com este investimento, os navios poderão manter os motores desligados enquanto estão acostados, reduzindo significativamente as emissões de gases poluentes e o ruído na região.
more: O cofinanciamento público pode atingir até 85% do valor investido pela Administração dos Portos do Douro, Leixões e Viana do Castelo, abrangendo os terminais de contentores e o terminal de passageiros da Doca 1 Norte.
O executivo sublinha que a medida se enquadra na estratégia de transição energética para o setor marítimo portuário nacional, promovendo o uso de energias limpas nas infraestruturas de transporte.

item.title: Custos do SIRESP descem e transferências ficam abaixo dos 26 milhões
item.snippet: Presidente da empresa gestora destaca decréscimo drástico nos custos por utilizador desde 2022.
body: O presidente da empresa que gere o SIRESP revelou que as transferências anuais efetuadas pelo Estado para o sistema de comunicações de emergência se mantêm sempre abaixo do teto máximo da indemnização compensatória.

Segundo o tenente-general Paulo Viegas Nunes, a verba oscila entre 19 e 26 milhões de euros, servindo para assegurar a operação contínua e a manutenção de uma infraestrutura com duas décadas de funcionamento.
more: O responsável apontou para uma redução expressiva nos custos por utilizador, que passaram de mais de três mil euros para valores na ordem dos 250 euros anuais.

No sentido de reforçar a transparência, a entidade gestora anunciou a publicação regular dos relatórios de execução orçamental na sua página oficial, permitindo um escrutínio mais direto sobre a gestão da rede.

item.title: Taxa de juro nos novos contratos de crédito à habitação sobe em setembro
item.snippet: Dados do INE mostram subida ligeira nas taxas e um novo acréscimo na prestação média mensal.
body: A taxa de juro implícita no conjunto dos contratos de crédito à habitação fixou-se em 3,194% no mês de setembro, traduzindo uma subida face ao período anterior, de acordo com os dados divulgados pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística.
Para os contratos celebrados nos últimos três meses, a taxa média avançou para 2,959%, impulsionando igualmente a prestação média paga pelas famílias.
more: A prestação média por contrato de habitação situou-se nos 423 euros, representando um acréscimo face ao mês precedente e ultrapassando os valores registados no período homólogo do ano passado.
Estes indicadores continuam a refletir a evolução das condições de financiamento no mercado imobiliário nacional, num contexto económico monitorizado de perto por analistas e decisores políticos.

item.title: Deputada australiana perde ambas as pernas após atropelamento
item.snippet: Helen Haines recupera de estado estável depois de um violento atropelamento em Wangaratta.
body: A deputada federal australiana Helen Haines perdeu as duas pernas na sequência de um atropelamento deliberado ocorrido perto do seu gabinete.
O marido da política confirmou que, apesar da gravidade dos ferimentos e da complexa intervenção cirúrgica, o estado clínico da deputada de 65 anos é agora estável.
more: As autoridades locais detiveram um homem de 43 anos, imputando-lhe vários crimes graves relacionados com o atropelamento, não descartando acusações adicionais.
A família tem apelado a donativos para organizações de apoio à infância em vez de flores, enquanto a comunidade local acompanha a recuperação da deputada.

item.title: Rússia liberta professor norte-americano em gestativa diplomática
item.snippet: Vladimir Putin anunciou a libertação de Stephen Hubbard durante encontro com o enviado dos EUA.
body: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, anunciou a libertação do professor norte-americano Stephen Hubbard, detido há quatro anos sob acusações de atividades mercenárias.
O anúncio ocorreu durante uma reunião em São Petersburgo com o enviado especial dos Estados Unidos, Steve Witkoff, tendo o cidadão norte-americano sido encaminhado para regressar ao seu país.
more: A administração norte-americana assinalou que a libertação ocorreu num contexto de respeito diplomático, sem necessidade de recorrer à habitual troca de prisioneiros.
As conversações entre as partes também abordaram perspetivas para potenciais negociações de paz e passos futuros relativos ao conflito na Ucrânia.
